The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with:
- Necrotic brown lesions at the margins
- Yellow/chlorotic wedge-shaped areas surrounding the necrosis
- V-shaped patterns from leaf margins inward
- Some small dark spots on the leaf surface

This strongly suggests a leaf disease. Let me check the part index, then view reference images.

Leaf-affecting classes from the index: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Early_Blight, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

The V-shaped yellowing at margins is most consistent with Verticillium_Wilt. Starting there first.
This Verticillium ref shows drooping/wilting without the distinct marginal necrosis pattern in the test image. Let me check Early_Blight and Late_Blight next.
Early Blight shows concentric ring spots - partially similar but the test image has more marginal necrosis patterns. Let me check Late_Blight.
That's a microscopy image - not useful. Let me check the other Late Blight leaf image and also branch out to other classes.
Late Blight shows dark greasy patches - doesn't match. Now checking Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, and Bacterial_Canker.
TSWV shows bronze-blue coloration with small spots - doesn't match. Let me check Septoria and Bacterial_Canker.
Septoria shows scattered small spots on a yellowing leaf - some similarities. Let me check Bacterial_Canker leaf and Verticillium second reference.
Bacterial Canker shows margin scorching - relevant. Let me now check more classes systematically.
This Verticillium Wilt reference (LeafNet_112) is very similar to the test image - brown marginal necrosis with yellow zones and green center. Strong match! Let me continue covering other classes.

This Early_Blight CDDM_1004 is nearly identical to the test image - same gray background, same leaf shape, same pattern of marginal necrosis with yellow halos. Very strong match! Let me cover remaining classes.
Bacterial Speck shows small scattered spots - doesn't match the large marginal necrosis pattern. Continuing with remaining classes.
CMV shows stunted/malformed leaves - doesn't match. Continuing.
Powdery Mildew shows white powdery deposits - doesn't match. I need 2 more views covering new classes. Let me check Anthracnose and Southern_Blight.

I've used all 16 reference views. Summary of findings:

**Best matches:**
- **Early_Blight/CDDM_1004.jpg**: Nearly identical to test image - same gray background, same leaf shape, same marginal necrosis with yellow halos, small dark spots. Extremely strong visual match.
- **Verticillium_Wilt/LeafNet_112.jpg**: Also shows marginal necrosis with yellow zones, but on a different substrate.

**Clear non-matches:** Late Blight (greasy patches), TSWV (bronze coloration), CMV (stunted/malformed), Gray Mold (tissue collapse), Powdery Mildew (white powder), Bacterial Speck (small scattered spots), Anthracnose (fruit lesion), Southern Blight (stem lesion).

**Decision:** The test image and Early_Blight CDDM_1004 are from the same CDDM dataset and show essentially identical patterns - a tomato leaf on a gray background with dark marginal necrosis surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos and some interior spots. The visual similarity is overwhelming. Per instructions, visual similarity to reference images takes precedence.
